title: LTS coexistence lanes and rollout choreography matrix
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a single source-of-truth matrix and choreographed rollout plan that defines LTS channel compatibility across runtime, API, SDKs, and Console. The goal is to enable parallel support lanes (current LTS, previous LTS, and latest stable), specify allowed breaking changes per lane, and codify automated rollout gates and rollback transitions so product and infra teams can test and deploy upgrades with predictable customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix spreadsheet exists and is versioned: rows = components (runtime, api, sdk-js, sdk-py, console), columns = channels (lts-previous, lts-current, stable, canary) with compatibility fingerprints
Runbook for release engineering and SRE describing preflight checks and automated rollback triggers is reviewed and approved
SDK compatibility shims documented and prototype patches landed in sdk-js and sdk-py repos
Console feature-flag gating pattern implemented and exercised in a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
End-to-end test matrix (integration + perf + canary telemetry) runs in CI for every channel promotion
tasks: Audit current versions across runtime, api, sdk-js, sdk-py, console and capture heuristics for incompatible changes
Design a compatibility fingerprinting format (semantic markers + runtime capability flags) and add to build artifacts
Populate canonical matrix in Drive and link to release-engineering repo as YAML reference
Implement preflight CI job that verifies matrix invariants before promotion
Create rollout gating automation in deployment pipelines and add observability hooks for latency/error regression detection
Draft rollback choreography that covers model variant fallbacks, cache invalidation, and client SDK downgrade paths
progress_updates: 2025-01-10: Ticket created after cross-team kickoff with PM, SDK and Console leads. Agreed on scope: matrix + rollout runbook + minimal code shims.

2025-01-18: Finished component audit. Spreadsheet (Drive) created: https://drive.google.com/example-lts-matrix (internal). Observed 3 places where runtime minor bumps cause SDK runtime API surface mismatch.

2025-01-22: Prototype of fingerprinting format committed to release-engineering repo: https://github.com/redwood/release-engineering/pull/412 (PR link). Initial format: {semver-major, runtime-capabilities:[kv-cache,v2-batching], api-flags:[structured-output, function-calls]}

2025-01-30: Design review with SDK leads. Decided to implement compatibility shim in sdk-js to gracefully handle missing runtime capability flags by falling back to polling-based batching for older runtimes.
2025-02-07: Created canary gating plan for console: feature-flag + rollout percentages + SLO monitors. Draft runbook is in Drive and needs SRE signoff.
2025-02-14: SRE suggested adding a latency slope detector (90th pct delta > 25% over baseline) as an automated rollback trigger; engineering agreed and started implementation (WIP).
decisions: Adopt a single compatibility fingerprint embedded in build artifacts rather than ad-hoc compatibility tables per repo
Keep 2 concurrent LTS lanes supported for 12 months each; older lanes enter maintenance mode (security + critical fixes only)
Use feature flags in Console to gate UI changes; require SDKs to provide graceful degradation for new features flagged by fingerprint
Automated rollback will be triggered by runbook-defined metric thresholds (error rate, latency slope, customer-facing errors) and a manual approval for non-obvious degradations
risks: SDKs may not be able to gracefully degrade for certain breaking runtime changes without larger refactors
Edge cases where model behavior (not infra) causes false-positive regressions in telemetry leading to unnecessary rollbacks
Coordination overhead across teams during a multi-lane rollout (runtime + API + SDK + Console) could delay promotions
Matrix drift if teams fail to update fingerprints during patch releases
testing_plan: Add matrix-driven integration tests that run combinations of (runtime build, api version, sdk version, console flag) in CI
Inject simulated regressions in canary to verify rollback automation responds (synthetic latency/error injection)
Add perf microbenchmarks for critical paths (KV cache hit/miss, batching throughput) and gate changes by 95th percentile thresholds
Run a staged customer-facing canary on a subset of low-risk orgs and monitor usage metrics for 7 days prior to full promotion
rollout_gates: Unit & integration tests green for matrix combinations
Canary deployment for 48 hours with no SLO breach
Automated telemetry checks: error-rate < baseline*1.2 and 90th-latency delta < 25%
Manual ops signoff if any non-trivial API change is shipped
SDK rolling-release: 25% clients -> 50% -> 100% with compatibility telemetry at each stage
rollback_plan: Tiered rollback: immediate automated rollback of runtime/service variant on SLO breach, followed by SDK re-routing to older API via fingerprint-aware client logic; operations runbook contains steps for cache flush, feature-flag reversal, and rolling back schema migrations. Post-rollback incident review required within 72 hours.
next_steps: Finish SRE implementation of latency slope detector and wire into rollback pipeline (owner: SRE team)
Land fingerprinting in runtime CI artifacts and update release pipeline to publish fingerprints
Coordinate SDK release windows and prepare communication plan for customers on expected compatibility guarantees
Schedule cross-team tabletop to rehearse rollback runbook on 2025-02-25
